identity.title: An ALMA [C II] Survey of 27 Quasars at z > 5.94

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present a survey of the [C ii] 158 $\mu$m line and underlying far–infrared (FIR) dust continuum emission in a sample of 27 $z\mathrel{\rlap{\lower 3pt \hbox{$\sim$}} \raise 2.0pt \hbox{$>$}}6$ quasars

coordinates.value: Listed per source in sample table (RA/Dec J2000)

distance_source.value: Pre-ALMA redshifts from Template/Lya/MgII/DLA; [CII] redshifts from ALMA spectral fits

question.value: What are the [C II] line and FIR dust continuum properties (luminosity, width, size, dynamical mass) of a homogeneous sample of z>5.94 quasar host galaxies?

evidence.quote: The size of the sample and the homogeneous data quality, together with the consistent analysis, allow us for the first time to study quasar host galaxies at the end of the reionization as a population.
The ALMA data set (program ID: 2015.1.01115.S) used in this study consists of short ($\sim8$ min on source) pointings
so that the [C ii] line falls in ALMA band 6 ($\sim 1.2$mm)

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: SPWs 0 and 1 cover expected [C II] (~3.6 GHz total); SPWs 2 and 3 around rest 1790 GHz

evidence.quote: The other two SPWs (2 and 3) covered rest-frame frequencies around 1790 GHz.
This results in a frequency coverage of $\sim 3.6$ GHz around the expected observed frequency of the [C ii] line
the [C ii] line ($\nu_0=1900.548$ GHz) is shifted to $\nu_{\rm obs}=253.406$ GHz
with the array in compact configuration with 38-49 12 m antennas
The synthesized beam size is typically $\sim 1.1''\times 0.8''$.
The typical rms noise is 0.5 mJy beam$^{-1}$ per 30 km s$^{-1}$ channel.
short ($\sim8$ min on source) pointings
Observations were carried out between 2016 January and July

what.value: [CII] luminosities, widths and continuum flux densities of 21 literature z>5.94 quasars (comparison sample)

evidence.quote: For these sources, we will use the line luminosity and width, and the dust continuum flux density derived in the papers quoted above.

method.value: Extract single-pixel spectrum at source; fit flat continuum + Gaussian

evidence.quote: We fit the spectra assuming a flat continuum emission from the dust, plus a Gaussian for the [C ii] line.

key_parameters.value: Detection if integrated flux exceeds 5 times lower-side uncertainty

evidence.quote: We consider a line detected if its integrated flux exceeds 5 times its lower-side uncertainty.

fitting.value: Metropolis MCMC; flat prior on peak frequency, Maxwellian (300 km/s) prior on width, broad Gaussian prior on line and continuum flux; median and 14-86% quantiles

evidence.quote: We adopt a flat prior for the line peak frequency, a Maxwellian distribution with a line width of 300 km s$^{-1}$

analysis_steps.goal: Measure line flux and size in 2D

method.value: Fit 2D Gaussian to continuum-subtracted line map in CASA, correct by 1/0.83 for line wings

evidence.quote: In the following, we define a source’s [C ii] flux through the measurement via the 2D spatial Gaussian fit, and scaling by a fixed $1/0.83\times$ factor

key_parameters.value: line map collapsed over peak ±1.4 sigma_line

evidence.quote: we collapse the data cube in the frequency range set by the line peak $\pm 1.4\,\sigma_{\rm line}$ from the best (spectral) fit

fitting.value: 2D Gaussian with free centroid, flux, deconvolved axes, PA, convolved with beam

evidence.quote: The modeled emission is then convolved with the observed beam, when fitting to the data.
the more extended objects tend to deviate from the 1–to–1 relation

evidence.quote: Basic estimates of the dynamical masses of the host galaxies give masses between $2\times10^{10}$ and $2\times10^{11}$ M$_\odot$

results_numeric.quantity: BH-to-host mass ratio for high S/N sources

evidence.quote: have a mass ratio of $>$0.03, i.e., $>$15 times higher than the value observed in the local universe

findings_qualitative.value: Stacked [CII] spectrum shows no deviation from a single Gaussian, so strong outflow like J1148+5251 is not common

evidence.quote: The strong outflow reported for an individual high–redshift quasar (cite: cicone15) thus does not appear to be a common feature of $z>6$ quasar hosts.

findings_qualitative.value: No Sigma_SFR approaches the Eddington limit (<100 Msun/yr/kpc2)

evidence.quote: are always $<100$ M$_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$ kpc$^{-2}$
